title: Adaptive KV-slab placement for tensor-split + pipeline-parallel GPUs
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: With mixed tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) model deployments, the KV cache footprint is spread across ranks in ways that interact badly with continuous batching and dynamic sequence lengths. Current slab sharding strategies either maximize locality (large contiguous slabs per GPU) or minimize cross-rank communication (consistent hashing), but neither adapts well to sudden shifts in hot prefixes or long-tail sequences. Goal: design and roll out an adaptive KV-slab placement and eviction system that reduces GPU memory fragmentation, minimizes cross-rank NCCL/host transfers during decode, preserves low tail latency for interactive workloads, and degrades gracefully for large-batch offline workloads.
proposal: 1) Slab taxonomy and metadata: break KV cache into small fixed-size slabs (configurable, default 1MB) with metadata about hotness, last-access-rank, and preferred-owner-rank. 2) Placement policy: at load time, prefer colocation of slabs with the TPU/TP shard executing corresponding attention layers when possible; for PP stages that sit on separate ranks, maintain a 'stage affinity' tag so slabs touched by a given pipeline stage prefer a small set of GPUs. 3) Hot-slab replication: replicate a small fraction of hottest slabs (top X%) to nearby ranks to eliminate the common NCCL round-trip on short prefixes; use a cheap bloom-based membership to avoid over-replication. 4) Background rebalance: use low-priority background tasks during idle GPU windows to move or shadow slabs, throttled by memory pressure and a budgeted NCCL byte cap. 5) Eviction: hybrid LRU-LFU per-slab with age-buckets; eviction prefers remote slabs first when memory constrained and demote hotness slowly to avoid thrash on oscillating workloads. 6) Runtime integration: expose placement hints to the kernel selector; pipeline scheduler uses placement to order micro-batches that reuse local slabs first. 7) Failure and fallback: if placement metadata inconsistent after a rank restart, fall back to consistent-hash lookup and lazily rebuild slab metadata. 8) Instrumentation: slab-level counters, move/replicate events, NCCL bytes per inference, and miss latency histograms.
design_decisions: Use fixed-size slabs to simplify rebalancing and prevent fragmentation; choice backed by perf sims showing 1MB slab size is a good trade-off for 8k context workloads
Replicate only top 1-3% hottest slabs because replication reduces tail latency but costs memory; this is tunable per-customer tier
Background rebalance is throttled aggressively to avoid interfering with live inference; prefer CPU-hosted movers that pin pages and use GPUDirect when available
Prefer local moves over remote fetch at decode time to keep tail latency predictable; decode-time remote fetch allowed only under explicit low-latency SLO exceptions
metrics_and_benchmarks: Baseline cluster: 4x A100-sXM GPUs, model: open-llama-7b, baseline continuous-batching throughput: 120 qps, p99 latency: 280ms, KV memory usage: 42GB total

Target: reduce cross-rank NCCL traffic by >=40% for interactive profile, reduce p99 latency by >=25ms for short-prefixed queries (<=64 tokens), maintain throughput within 5% of baseline for large offline batches
Memory goals: reduce peak per-GPU KV fragmentation by 20% and keep warm-replica overhead <=6% of total KV memory
Bench harnesses: perf-runner cluster (link below) includes random prefix mixes, long-tail (1% > 1k tokens), and mixed-mode (interactive + batch) workloads
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation and offline cost model (2 weeks) - run slab placement sims on production traces stored in S3 to validate hot-slab percentile thresholds
Phase 1: Feature gated runtime in staging (canary) with telemetry only (3 weeks) - no replication, only placement hints emitted, compare predicted vs actual misses
Phase 2: Canary with hot-slab replication enabled on dedicated cluster (2 weeks) - measure NCCL reduction and p99 latency improvements
Phase 3: Gradual rollout to low-traffic customers with ability to opt-out, monitor key metrics for 2 weeks before wider availability
Rollback: global gate to disable placement hints and replication; fallback to consistent-hash slab lookup (instant), and automated alerting if p99 increases by >20%
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end functional tests that verify slab movement, replication, and eviction under synthetic load
Bench results meet targets in metrics_and_benchmarks for the staging cluster
No regression in throughput (>95% of baseline) on large-batch offline workloads during canary
Dashboard panels for slab moves, NCCL bytes, p50/p95/p99 decode latencies, and memory fragmentation are added to runtime-1.22 release dashboard
Security review completed and sign-off if customer_impact is not none
notes: 2026-01-15: Kickoff with runtime, infra, and perf teams. Agreed to prototype with 1MB slabs and a conservative hot-replication fraction (1%).
2026-01-22: Diego ran first trace-based simulator; initial sims show 35% reduction in remote fetches on interactive trace but 7% additional memory used for replicas.
2026-02-03: Design review with PM (Lina Kovács) - requested clearer failover semantics for rank restarts and a canary gating plan.
2026-02-28: Security flagged KMS access for slab metadata encryption at rest - added requirement to use envelope encryption for metadata blobs.
2026-03-05: Perf team found a regression in micro-batch ordering when placement hints are missing; added fallback micro-batch sorter in runtime scheduler.
Action items: implement bloom membership for replicated slab lookups, add per-slab move budgeter, add GC hook for long-unused slabs
